items.title: 52222_Marshall Royal oral history interview
items.q: So, that was the first regular job that I worked with, with Lawrence Brown, when I was 16 years old.

ctx.x: Lawrence worked there with -- Lawrence was the a trombone player, I was the saxophone player and Lawrence's brother was the piano player. Alton Red (PHONETIC), drum, Harold Erroll Scott (PHONETIC) was the trumpet player and the leader of the band was a fellow by the name of Atwell Rose (PHONETIC)
and he was a very, very fine violin player, just a great violin player. So, that was the first regular job that I worked with, with Lawrence Brown, when I was 16 years old.
You said Lawrence was putting his age up -- you told me this off the tape -- putting his age up in order to get some of these jobs in those days.

items.title: 52986_Lawrence Brown oral history interview
items.q: I know Marshall Royal was one.

ctx.x: Whom did you play with with Curtis Moseby?
Oh, gee I can't remember half the names. I can't even hardly remember the personnel of the band. I know Marshall Royal was one. And gee, I don't remember too many of the fellows.

Another interesting thing in all of these bands at that time was we played for the dancing of the patrons on the floor. Then between sets we would play for the entertainers who went out on the floor and dispersed among the audiences, and would sing individual songs at the individual tables.
